validated_results.title: Food consumption, meat cooking methods and diet diversity and the risk of bladder cancer.
validated_results.reason: Italian case-control study reporting an adjusted OR for milk/yogurt (dairy) consumption and incident bladder cancer risk.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quartile of milk/yogurt consumption

sample_size.excerpt: Data were derived from an Italian multicentre case-control study, conducted between 2003 and 2014, including 690 bladder cancer cases and 665 frequency-matched controls.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 690 + 665 = 1355

cases.excerpt: Data were derived from an Italian multicentre case-control study, conducted between 2003 and 2014, including 690 bladder cancer cases and 665 frequency-matched controls.

effect_size.excerpt: Comparing the highest versus the lowest quartiles, consumption of vegetables (OR = 0.62; 95%CI: 0.44-0.88) and milk/yogurt (OR = 0.62; 95%CI: 0.44-0.87) reduced the risk of bladder cancer.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Comparing the highest versus the lowest quartiles, consumption of vegetables (OR = 0.62; 95%CI: 0.44-0.88) and milk/yogurt (OR = 0.62; 95%CI: 0.44-0.87) reduced the risk of bladder cancer.

comparison.excerpt: Comparing the highest versus the lowest quartiles

design.excerpt: Data were derived from an Italian multicentre case-control study

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Odds ratios (ORs) and the corresponding 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs) for various dietary aspects were estimated by unconditional logistic regression models adjusted for energy intake
